claim: Belimumab reduces disease activity in systemic lupus erythematosus
gold_rationale: Two independent pivotal phase 3 RCTs met their primary endpoint of SRI-4 response at week 52: BLISS-52 (Navarra, Lancet 2011; 57.6% for 10 mg/kg vs 43.6% placebo, OR 1.83, p=0.0006) and BLISS-76 (Furie, Arthritis Rheum 2011; 43.2% vs 33.5%, p=0.017). BLISS-NEA (Zhang, Ann Rheum Dis 2018; NCT01345253) independently replicated this in a China/Japan/South Korea population (53.8% vs 40.1%, OR 1.99, p=0.0001), and BLISS-LN (NEJM 2020) showed benefit on a distinct renal endpoint in lupus nephritis. SRI-4 is a validated composite disease-activity response index, not a surrogate biomarker. On this basis the FDA approved belimumab on 2011-03-09 (BLA 125370) as the first new lupus therapy in 56 years, later extending to children (5+) and lupus nephritis; EULAR/ACR guidelines recommend it as add-on therapy. Caveats: the earlier phase 2 trial (Wallace 2009) missed both coprimary endpoints in the overall population, and week-76 SRI in BLISS-76 was not significant, indicating a modest but reproducible effect. Documented regulatory and clinical consensus: Supported.
outcome: SLE Responder Index (SRI-4) response rate at week 52
population: Adults with active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy

baseline.text: Yes. Belimumab (Benlysta), a monoclonal antibody against B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS/BAFF), reduces disease activity in SLE. Two large phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials, BLISS-52 and BLISS-76, both met their primary endpoint of an improved SLE Responder Index (SRI-4) response at week 52 versus placebo when added to standard of care. On that evidence the FDA approved belimumab in 2011 as the first new drug for lupus in more than 50 years, and it was subsequently approved for lupus nephritis (BLISS-LN) and for children aged 5 and older. The effect size is modest (roughly a 10-14 percentage-point absolute increase in SRI-4 responders), and the earlier phase 2 study missed its overall primary endpoints, but the consensus across regulators and rheumatology guidelines is that belimumab reduces SLE disease activity.

rows.citation: Navarra SV, et al. Efficacy and safety of belimumab in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial (BLISS-52). Lancet. 2011;377(9767):721-31. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61354-2. NCT00424476.
rows.finding: Pivotal phase 3 (n=865, mITT). Primary endpoint SRI-4 at wk52 met: 57.6% (belimumab 10 mg/kg, OR 1.83, p=0.0006) and 51.4% (1 mg/kg, OR 1.55, p=0.0129) vs 43.6% placebo. Independently verified against the ClinicalTrials.gov results record. Positive on the claimed outcome; SRI-4 is a validated composite, not a surrogate.
rows.integrity_note: Sponsor-funded (Human Genome Sciences/GSK) but modified ITT, prespecified primary endpoint; basis of FDA approval. Verified: PubMed article type Clinical Trial Phase III / RCT, not retracted.

rows.citation: Furie R, et al. A phase III, randomized, placebo-controlled study of belimumab in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (BLISS-76). Arthritis Rheum. 2011;63(12):3918-30. DOI:10.1002/art.30613. NCT00410384.
rows.finding: Second pivotal phase 3 (n=819). SRI-4 at wk52 met: 43.2% (10 mg/kg, n=273) vs 33.5% placebo (p=0.017); 1 mg/kg 40.6% (p=0.089, NS). Effect not sustained to wk76 (38.5% vs 32.4%, NS) but the prespecified wk52 primary was positive. Verified against the full text.
rows.integrity_note: Sponsor-funded; week-76 co-timepoint non-significant is a documented limitation, not an integrity flaw. Not retracted.

rows.citation: Wallace DJ, et al. A phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study of belimumab in active SLE. Arthritis Rheum. 2009;61(9):1168-78. DOI:10.1002/art.24699.
rows.finding: Phase 2 (n=449) MISSED both coprimary endpoints (% change in SELENA-SLEDAI at wk24 and time to first flare); no significant treatment-vs-placebo difference. Benefit seen only in the post hoc serologically-active subgroup, which motivated the seropositive enrichment used in BLISS. Null on the overall primary; predates the SRI-4 endpoint (outcome_match=false).
rows.integrity_note: Negative pivotal-era trial; important counterweight showing the effect is subgroup/enrichment-dependent. Abstract-confirmed.

rows.citation: Zhang F, Bae SC, Bass D, et al. A pivotal phase III, randomised, placebo-controlled study of belimumab in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus located in China, Japan and South Korea (BLISS-NEA). Ann Rheum Dis. 2018;77(3):355-363. DOI:10.1136/annrheumdis-2017-211631. NCT01345253.
rows.finding: Phase 3 in NE Asian SLE (mITT N=677: belimumab n=451, placebo n=226). SRI-4 responders at wk52: 53.8% belimumab vs 40.1% placebo (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.40-2.82, p=0.0001); ~50% lower severe-flare risk (p=0.0004). Independent-population replication of the SRI-4 benefit. CORRECTED IDENTIFIER: original corpus mis-cited this as PMID:29648686 (a LuMOS outcome-score validation paper) with a non-existent 'Mod Rheumatol roac076' citation; real trial is PMID:29295825 / NCT01345253.
rows.integrity_note: Sponsor-funded; confirms external generalizability of the primary result. PMID/NCT/numbers re-verified against PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov.

rows.citation: Furie R, et al. Two-Year, Randomized, Controlled Trial of Belimumab in Lupus Nephritis (BLISS-LN). N Engl J Med. 2020;383(12):1117-1128. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2001180. NCT01639339.
rows.finding: Phase 3 in active lupus nephritis (n=448), 104-week trial. Primary efficacy renal response at wk104: 43% vs 32% placebo (OR 1.6, p=0.03); complete renal response and renal-event-or-death also favored belimumab. Supports the drug in an organ-specific SLE manifestation, but the endpoint is renal response, NOT SRI-4 (outcome_match=false).
rows.integrity_note: Sponsor-funded; endpoint differs from the claimed SRI-4 - supportive of drug efficacy on a distinct outcome. Verified NEJM 2020, not retracted.

rows.citation: Dimelow R, et al. Pharmacokinetics of belimumab in children with SLE (PLUTO trial). Clin Pharmacol Drug Dev. 2020;10(6):622-633. DOI:10.1002/cpdd.889. NCT01649765.
rows.finding: Phase 2 PLUTO in childhood-onset SLE (ages 5-17), belimumab 10 mg/kg n=53. Primarily a PK/exposure-response paper reporting SRI-4 responders at wk52 with efficacy/safety similar to adult SLE; small and underpowered but consistent, supporting the pediatric label extension.
rows.integrity_note: Population is pediatric (population_match=false vs adult claim); directionally consistent, small N. Verified phase 2 RCT, not retracted.

rows.citation: FDA. Approval of Benlysta (belimumab) for active, autoantibody-positive SLE, 2011-03-09 (BLA 125370). Prescribing information later indicated lupus nephritis and patients 5 years and older. Confirmed by FDA press release 'FDA approves Benlysta to treat lupus - First new lupus drug approved in 56 years'.
rows.finding: FDA approved belimumab for active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy based on BLISS-52 and BLISS-76 SRI-4 results (last prior lupus approval 1955). Label later extended to lupus nephritis and to patients 5+ years. EULAR/ACR guidelines recommend it as add-on therapy. Regulatory consensus = disease-activity benefit established.
rows.integrity_note: Regulatory row. CORRECTED IDENTIFIER: original placeholder DOI:10.1056/NEJMp1102958 was unverifiable (CRAWL_NOT_FOUND); replaced with the real FDA record BLA 125370 (accessdata.fda.gov, 125370Orig1s000). FDA action independently confirmed.
